**Hydrogen – Key Properties** | Property | Value / Description | |----------|---------------------| | **Atomic number** | 1 | | **Isotopes** | H‑1 (protium), H‑2 (deuterium), H‑3 (tritium) | | **Molecular form** | Diatomic gas (H₂) under normal conditions | | **State at room temperature** | Colorless, odorless, tasteless gas | | **Density (STP)** | 0.0899 g L⁻¹ (≈1/14th that of air) | | **Melting point** | –259.16 °C (−434.49 °F) | | **Boiling point** | –252.87 °C (–423.17 °F) | | **Enthalpy of formation (ΔH°f)** | 0 kJ mol⁻¹ (by definition for elemental H₂) | | **Entropy (S°)** | 130.68 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ | | **Gibbs free energy (ΔG°f)** | 0 kJ mol⁻¹ (by definition for elemental H₂) | | **Ionization energy** | 13.598 eV (first ionization) | | **Electron affinity** | –0.754 eV | | **Electronegativity (Pauling)** | 2.20 | | **Covalent radius** | ~31 pm | | **Van der Waals radius** | ~120 pm | | **Bond dissociation energy (H–H)** | 436 kJ mol⁻¹ | | **Standard molar volume (at STP)** | 22.414 L mol⁻¹ | | **Reactivity** | Highly reactive; reduces many oxides; reacts explosively with O₂ or air in presence of spark/heat | | **Uses** | • Fuel (rocket propellant, fuel cells)
• Industrial feedstock (ammonia via Haber‑Bosch, methanol, hydrides)
• Electrolytic production of metals
• Chemical synthesis (hydrogenation, dehydrogenation reactions)
• Medical imaging (PET tracers with tritium)
• Semiconductor manufacturing (cleaning, doping) | --- ### Quick Facts * **Lightest element** – lowest atomic mass (1.008 u for protium). * **Most abundant element in the Universe** – ~75 % of baryonic mass. * **Non‑metallic diatomic gas** – forms H₂ molecules under ambient conditions. * **Highly flammable** – explosive mixtures with air/O₂ from 4 % to 75 % concentration. * **Key industrial role** – central to the Haber‑Bosch process for ammonia, which fuels global agriculture. * **Energy carrier** – potential clean fuel source when produced via renewable electrolysis. These properties make hydrogen unique among elements, influencing its behavior in chemistry, physics, and engineering applications.
